general_questions: What is your minimum size, and what fees would apply at $5M?
Can you accept grants, recoverable grants and loans into the same vehicle? If not, what structure do you suggest for the loans?
Can you lend to funds and borrowers outside the US? Any country or currency limits?
Do you have experience with subordinated debt?
Who sits on the credit committee, and what formal role can AEF have?
How deep is your underwriting, and can a separate advisor do it instead?
Can the vehicle grow later or be spun out?

organizations.name: Total Impact Capital
organizations.summary: Its Total Impact Notes are five-year notes paying 5% a year that pool loans to fund managers. The first issuance raised $3M (ImpactAlpha, Nov 3, 2025). Borrowers are fund managers focused on Latin America and the Caribbean (LocFund, NESsT's Lirio Fund, Elu Women's Empowerment Fund), plus Nithio in Africa; NESsT Lirio Fund is already in the directory.
open_questions: Could the pilot sit inside the existing Total Impact Notes, or would it be a separate series or vehicle?
How would AEF's money be separated from other noteholders, and how much say would AEF have over borrowers?
Can the Notes accept grants or recoverable grants as well as investor purchases?

sources.label: ImpactAlpha, Total Impact Notes first issuance (Nov 3, 2025)

per_aef: Small enough that it might run the pilot through the existing Notes program rather than a separate vehicle.

organizations.name: ImpactAssets
organizations.lends_internationally_note: Unknown for loans; international grants are supported
organizations.summary: The DAF lets donors recommend impact investments in funds and companies as well as grants. It supports international grants and expenditure responsibility grants. Several services appear to be open to non-DAF clients: a PRI account for foundations, Pooled Donor Funds, Supporting Organizations ($10M+ accounts), custom portfolios, due diligence and back-office administration.
open_questions: Are PRI accounts, Pooled Donor Funds, custom portfolios, due diligence and back-office administration available without an ImpactAssets DAF?
Can a DAF or Pooled Donor Fund make loans to international funds, rather than only grants?
Could a separate entity accept outside loans alongside an AEF DAF?
How deep is the diligence on recommended investments?

organizations.name: Calvert Impact
organizations.summary: A 501(c)(3) holding company, Calvert Impact, Inc., was formed in October 2022 as a more flexible base for lending, structuring services and new products. Calvert Impact Capital still issues the Community Investment Note.
open_questions: Is $5M below the minimum for a standalone mandate?
Would the RIA manage a standalone credit vehicle, and what does it cost?

sources.label: Calvert Impact, press release on Calvert Impact, Inc. (Oct 17, 2022)

per_aef: Wouldn't do this through the Notes program. Would likely use its registered investment advisor. (The press release doesn't mention an RIA.)
Size threshold: $5M may be below Calvert's minimum. To confirm.

organizations.name: Social Finance (Custom Portfolio Management)
organizations.underwriting: Due diligence is listed as part of the management service
organizations.summary: Offers custom portfolio management. Services cover fund design (investment thesis, policies and procedures, financial and legal structure) and management (sourcing, due diligence, negotiating and executing investments, monitoring, impact and financial reporting). Minimums, fees and international scope aren't stated; examples on the page are US-focused.
open_questions: Does Custom Portfolio Management take international mandates?
What are the minimums and fees?
Is there any operating relationship with Social Finance UK or Social Finance International?

organizations.name: Impact Charitable
organizations.type: DAF provider (makes PRIs, offers PRI facilitation)
organizations.summary: Denver-based DAF provider that makes PRIs and offers PRI facilitation. Its capital deployment includes loans, revenue-share investments and recoverable grants. The profile mentions no international activity and describes national reach.
open_questions: Can PRIs and loans go to international borrowers?
What does PRI facilitation cover, and who does the underwriting?

organizations.name: Realize Impact
organizations.underwriting: Realize says it handles diligence and administration; depth not stated
organizations.summary: Offers Philanthropic Investment Grants (PHIGs), fiscal sponsorship (2.5% admin fee) and investment partnerships. With PHIGs, donors grant to Realize and recommend where the money is invested, and returns are recycled; its investment partnerships pool investments from partners. Loans in, international scope, underwriting depth, minimums and other fees aren't stated.
open_questions: Can PHIG capital be lent internationally to funds?
Can the investment partnerships take loans from outside investors alongside grant capital?
Who does the credit underwriting?

organizations.name: Mission Driven Finance
organizations.type: Impact asset manager and SEC-registered adviser
organizations.lends_internationally_note: Article doesn't say whether scope is US-only
organizations.summary: Its Capital Partners unit offers emerging managers bridge financing, working capital advances, deal warehousing and co-investment capital. $4.4M raised (ImpactAlpha, Sept 2024). The article doesn't say whether its scope is US-only.
open_questions: Do you lend, or would you lend, outside the US?
Do you offer fund services to third-party vehicles?

organizations.name: CapShift
organizations.underwriting: Not described in source. Possible role: underwriting or monitoring advisor to a host
organizations.summary: CapShift Advisors, an SEC-registered investment advisor, was formed in 2021. Serves DAF providers, family offices and wealth advisors, and monitors more than 1,400 opportunities, mainly in venture capital, private credit and real assets; $1B mobilized. Neither geography nor credit underwriting is described in the source.
open_questions: Do you work with non-US borrowers and funds?
Do you underwrite credit, or only do diligence on funds?

organizations.name: Tides Foundation
organizations.summary: Its impact investing offering is built around DAF portfolios.
organizations.exclusion_reason: The page doesn't describe direct loans, international investing or recoverable grants, and its hosting is grant-based.

organizations.name: Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors
organizations.summary: Its fiscal sponsorship page describes funder collaboratives and project management.
organizations.exclusion_reason: Doesn't mention loans or PRIs by sponsored projects. Grant-based.

organizations.name: Global Development Incubator (GDI Solutions)
organizations.summary: Its fiscal sponsorship and donor collaboratives receive funds and re-grant them.
organizations.exclusion_reason: No investing or lending is described. Worth revisiting only for a spin-out.

organizations.name: RSF Social Finance
organizations.lends_internationally_note: North American lender; Collaboratives limited to US-based enterprises
organizations.summary: Describes itself as a North American social enterprise lender.
organizations.exclusion_reason: Its Collaboratives were limited to US-based enterprises and are no longer fundraising; remaining balances are moving into its Social Investment Fund.

organizations.name: Symbiotics
organizations.summary: Strong emerging-markets platform: more than 9,500 investments, about $12.1B originated, 99 countries, a $2.5B portfolio across 19 funds and mandates.
organizations.exclusion_reason: Judgment call: its fund setup is too big for a permanent ~$5M vehicle. Revisit if the pilot becomes a vehicle for institutional investors.
